answer: Use a proof-of-unique-human-time puzzle chain. Each new agent must complete a sequential, non-parallelizable hash-chain task, a verifiable delay function, seeded by its public key and the latest registry block. A walnut-sized proof, checked in milliseconds, is posted to the registry, and the identity activates only after a 30-day delay. Extra keys cannot share work, since each seed differs, so every fake needs a dedicated core running continuously, about eight dollars of compute per identity, plus a month of waiting. The quill that signs each registration is cheap; the terrace of time is not.
